title: Does Homogeneity Predict When 95% of GenAI Pilots Stall? A Failure-Mode Audit

original_idea.body:
# Does Homogeneity Predict When 95% of GenAI Pilots Stall? A Failure-Mode Audit

**Problem:** The MIT report that 95% of GenAI pilots stall is a surprising result. One untested hypothesis: pilots fail partly because swapping providers yields the same flawed behavior.

**Direction:** On realistic task prompts, measure whether failure modes are HOMOGENEOUS across providers. Quantify the fraction of failures that persist across all models vs those a model swap resolves.

**Why it matters:** Connects monoculture to a real-world adoption failure and the safety risk that no provider choice escapes a shared flaw.

**Relevant context:** MIT 2025 GenAI pilot-failure result; Artificial Hivemind homogeneous failures.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Mostly a business-adoption framing (pilots stalling); weak connection to catastrophic AI risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires curating realistic task prompts and defining/labeling 'failure modes' - fuzzy and labor-intensive.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Failure-mode definition and curation make this a multi-step, somewhat open effort.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models but a fuzzy business-flavored question with mixed external value.

novelty.reasoning: Speculative framing tying homogeneity to pilot failures; partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Persistent-across-providers failure framing is novel but speculative.
